findings.evidence: Kinematics/Basic.lean:31-43 adds `namespace Bilin … end Bilin` under `namespace Kinematics`; Tensors/Basic.lean:94-208 is `namespace Bilin` under `namespace Tensors`, containing `reflect` (156), `reflect_apply_self` (177), `reflect_isometry` (190), `det_reflect` (199). grep for the new lemma returns only Tensors/Basic.lean:637 and Tensors/ParityOdd.lean:154,155,177, all written with the bare `Bilin.` prefix.
findings.fix: Declare the lemma in the existing `Bilin` namespace of `Tensors/Tensors.Basic` next to `reflect_*`/`det_reflect` (its only two callers, Tensors/Basic.lean and Tensors/ParityOdd.lean, are both downstream of it) and drop the new `namespace Bilin` block from `Kinematics/Basic.lean`, so `Bilin.*` names one namespace.
findings.issue: `apply_eq_zero_of_apply_eq_self_of_apply_eq_neg` is put in a newly opened `namespace Bilin` in `Kinematics` (full name `Kinematics.Bilin.…`), while every other bilinear-form helper lives in the `Bilin` namespace of `Tensors` (`Tensors.Bilin.reflect`, `reflect_apply_self`, `reflect_isometry`, the new `det_reflect`). Both are written `Bilin.…` at the call sites, so the same prefix resolves to two different namespaces — at Tensors/Basic.lean:637-640 `Bilin.apply_eq_zero_of_apply_eq_self_of_apply_eq_neg` (Kinematics.Bilin) and `Bilin.reflect_apply_of_orthogonal` (Tensors.Bilin) sit in one expression — and any future lemma added to both sides becomes an ambiguous name.

summary: Names describe their conclusions in standard terminology, suffixes match statement strength, and no notation is added; the earlier `lMuNuOdd` finding is withdrawn since that declaration is present in the tree. The remaining defect is that the new helper lands in a second namespace also called `Bilin`, so `Bilin.*` now denotes two different namespaces for the same type.
